items.headline: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
items.blurb: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
items.text: For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place. With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance. The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.

items.headline: Why a trio of experts alleges Jeffrey Epstein did not die by suicide
items.blurb: A new report alleges that injuries on Epstein's body were overlooked by medical examiners during his 2019 autopsy.
items.text: A trio of experts has released a report casting doubt on whether convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein died by suicide in his jail cell in 2019, as a medical examiner in the United States previously ruled. In documents obtained by Al Jazeera and other media outlets, Michael Freeman, Anders Eriksson and Itiel Dror – a forensic scientist, a forensic pathologist and a cognitive scientist – said the injuries on Epstein’s body were “most consistent with homicidal strangulation”, not suicide. “The pattern, distribution, and multitude of injuries are not explained by a suicidal hanging,” their report reads. Instead, they suggest Epstein was first assaulted and then strangled, providing an alternative narrative to the medical examiner’s 2019 report. The cause of Epstein’s death has long been a source of controversy and conspiracy theories. A wealthy businessman, Epstein cultivated a range of high-profile relationships with leaders in politics, industry, academia and the arts. items.headline: 'The drones don't fly here' - BBC reports from Ukraine's new front line
items.blurb: Ukrainian forces are fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet tunnel in the Kharkiv region.
items.text: There's a new front in the war in Ukraine, and it is underground. For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region. With a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance. Going underground is now the "only option", says Zanuda, who has helped plan Ukraine's tunnel operation and calls it a new world of fighting. But, he acknowledges, it is hard. "On the surface you always have some room to manoeuvre, but here you can only engage the enemy head-on." The journey to get to this subterranean battleground in the Kharkiv region only reinforced the dangers on the ground: a high-speed move by vehicle across open fields, followed by a long march across muddy ground – accompanied by Ukrainian troops with their weapons loaded, ready to shoot down Russian drones.

items.headline: Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres
items.blurb: No state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.
items.text: When the judges of the International Court of Justice read out their verdict in the seven-year-old genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar on Thursday, they could make history. In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia. But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide. "It would be a judgment of landmark importance if The Gambia were to win this case," says Arsalan Suleman, the lawyer leading the case against Myanmar at the court. "It would give renewed vitality to the 1948 Genocide Convention and to the notion of international legal accountability for crimes committed by a state." items.headline: DGCA proposes separate registration system for prototype, production aircraft
items.blurb: Under the proposed framework, a common pool of registration marks will be created for production and prototype aircraft
items.text: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has proposed a separate registration mechanism for aircraft undergoing production and prototype testing, allowing manufacturers to obtain dedicated registration marks for test flights without entering the aircraft in India’s regular civil aircraft register. The proposal is part of a revised set of Civil Aviation Requirements (CAR) governing aircraft registration and de-registration, which also seeks to tighten documentation requirements for aircraft taken on dry lease and prevent the reallocation of registration marks once an aircraft has been entered in the Indian Civil Aircraft Register. Under the proposed framework, a common pool of registration marks will be created for production and prototype aircraft. Applicants will be required to apply through the DGCA’s e-GCA portal using a separate application form and submit production approval documents. These could include a letter of agreement issued by the Aircraft Engineering Directorate or production organisation approval issued by the DGCA or a foreign civil aviation authority. The registration fee will be calculated on the basis of the aircraft’s maximum take-off weight (MTOW), as specified in its type certificate data sheet

items.headline: Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035 worldwide: Pew research
items.blurb: The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070
items.text: Muslims comprise 15.2% of India’s religious composition in 2020, and that share is set to rise to 19.6% by 2070. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto Islam is projected to be the world's largest religion by 2035, surpassing Christianity, according to a new study released by the Pew Research Centre on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). Pew said if current trends continue, there will be more than 3.6 billion Muslims and just under three billion Christians worldwide by 2070. The absolute number of Hindus in India and worldwide will rise from 1.2 billion in 2020 to 1.4 billion by 2070. But the rest of the world's population -- all non-Hindus -- will grow at an even faster rate. As a result, Hindus will shrink slightly as a share of the global population, falling from 15% in 2020 to 14% in 2070. The world's total population is projected to increase by 29% between 2020 and 2070, with Christians growing by 30% and Muslims by 80%. However, the court agreed to hear the Enforcement Directorate’s (ED’s) challenge to the Allahabad High Court order granting him relief. The release warrant reached Dasna jail at around 4.30 pm, following which formalities were completed and Khan was allowed to walk out. He left for his hometown Rampur. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav described his release as a victory of truth and expressed confidence that Khan would continue to get justice. “Truth has triumphed. We have complete faith in the judiciary. The money raised surpassed SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June. Elon Musk’s company raised $75 billion initially and a total of $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their overallotment. The round comprises a mix of primary and secondary capital. The proceeds will be used to expand Style Union's physical store network across key metropolitan markets. This will take the retailer beyond its southern India base into western and northern markets, Nexon Omniverse said in a press release. Founded in 2022 by Ekta Biyani, wife of businessman Rakesh Biyani, Style Union is a fast-fashion and value-retail brand that offers affordable everyday apparel, athleisure, ethnic wear, accessories and makeup for men, women and children through online and offline channels. The company currently operates 200 stores across Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Delhi-NCR. items.text: Boba Bhai has raised $18 Mn in a Series B round led by Left Lane Capital, with participation from BIG Capital and other existing investors The funding will support the startup's expansion to 250–300 outlets, entry into new markets and its ambition to build a multi-brand QSR platform Founded in 2023, Boba Bhai operates 120 outlets, serves 3.5 Lakh monthly orders and reported ₹70 Cr in FY26 revenue Quick service restaurant (QSR) chain Boba Bhai has raised $18 Mn (about ₹168 Cr) in its Series B funding round led by US-based Left Lane Capital. The round also saw participation from BIG Capital as well as existing backers including Titan Capital. Speaking with Inc42, founder Dhruv Kohli said that the round comprised both a primary deal and a small secondary component. The fresh capital will primarily be deployed towards store expansion, strengthening its senior leadership team and building new consumer food brands under Boba Bhai Ventures. “Expansion is the sole priority. As we have more capital now, we will double down on existing markets while also entering new markets,” Kohli said.

items.blurb: PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal will step down as Executive Vice Chairman and Whole Time Director on March 31, 2027. He will continue on the company's board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director from April 1, 2027.
items.text: PB Fintech co-founder Alok Bansal will step down as Executive Vice Chairman and Whole Time Director on March 31, 2027. He will continue on the company's board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director from April 1, 2027. The company's board approved the change in designation at its meeting held on November 18, 2026. Bansal has expressed his desire to step back from day-to-day executive responsibilities for personal reasons, according to a regulatory filing. Bansal co-founded Policybazaar with Yashish Dahiya in 2008. Over the past 18 years, he has played a key role in the company's strategy, fundraising, corporate development and investor relations, including its public listing in 2021. PB Fintech reported a 43% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 193 crore in Q2 FY27, compared to Rs 135 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue from operations grew 35% to Rs 2,178 crore during the quarter from Rs 1,614 crore in Q2 FY26. items.blurb: The Premier League resumes on Saturday with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Man Utd in the relegation zone. But is it too early to be worried?
items.text: Despite being only 10 games into the season, sitting in the relegation zone even at this early stage is more worrying than you might think. But with how tight the Premier League table is, this could also be one of the fiercest relegation battles we have seen in a long time. Two of the current bottom three, Crystal Palace and Manchester United , will resume their campaigns at the weekend with new managers after appointing Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino respectively. Sunderland , wedged between the pair in 19th, have not pressed the panic button and have kept faith with Regis le Bris. But is it too early to worry? We look at what the stats tell us about relegation battles in the past and what we can learn for the months ahead. items.text: New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0–1 Test series defeat in 1980. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1–0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. items.blurb: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit, rather than reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. The short answer is AI, but not in the way you might expect.
items.text: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained Wednesday why he offered buyouts to 60,000 of his employees in October, essentially urging them to voluntarily quit instead of reducing the workforce via another massive layoff. Short answer: AI, but not, he insists, in the way you might expect. He’s not saying he’s replacing employees with AI, especially software engineers. He’s saying he’s reorganizing Microsoft into a company where everyone uses AI to do their work, and their jobs become focused on managing that AI. The buyout was “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices,” he told Andrew Ross Sorkin during the DealBook Summit. “Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he

Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack . You go to the movies and see Sam Altman being played with nauseating intensity by Andrew Garfield, and go back home to find that Elon Musk has released a Grok-fied version of The Odyssey . You try to watch it, but it feels like a long, unskippable mobile ad. In a way, the whole world kind of feels that way now: Like a modern Odysseus, you are cursed to roam AI-infested waters, dueling with machine gods and monsters, trying to find your way back to somewhere that feels like home. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet.” In other words: The smartification of the economy, in which much of the world’s “dumb” devices were hooked up to the internet, is now causing tremendous headaches. The conversation took place against the backdrop of a wave of recent large-scale outages — including one involving Microsoft Outlook. Others have involved the NSA, the FFA, and Apple. items.blurb: With MyMems , Wright says he wants to "turn the simulation inward."
items.text: The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright ( SimCity , The Sims ) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA . Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories. MyMems , which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turning the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning . items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

items.text: If someone handed you $8,300 every second, what would you do? That’s how much pure profit Nvidia now makes. By the time you finish reading this paragraph, Nvidia will likely have cleared $45,000 and change. It’s easy to look at Nvidia, a company that just lost its visionary founder CEO due to a series of scandals , and think that the company and maybe the entire AI industry are in terrible trouble. Perhaps so ? But I want you to understand: Nvidia isn’t your average semi-successful company that might tempt a new CEO to fix things that are broken. It is a company so staggeringly, mind-bogglingly successful it’ll do everything in its power not to rock the boat. There is so much money at stake. It’s so much money that when I heard about Jensen Huang’s resignation, my first thought was: I need a way to visualize this jaw-dropping amount of money for you . I want to show you that Nvidia has risen so far, so fast, that rival chipmakers AMD, Intel, and Qualcomm barely qualify as competition now.

items.text: On Friday, a petition to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia began circulating on social media, and by Monday it listed some notable signatories, including Elon Musk and several influential Nvidia researchers. But comb through the more than 115,000 names and you’ll notice a significant faction of Huang’s supporters—higher-ups from Hugging Face, a hub for sharing AI models, and venture capital firms Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia Capital—come from a particular slice of the tech world. These names have a vested interest in the development of open-source AI, models that, unlike ChatGPT or Claude, can be downloaded and run independent of large tech companies. Supporters of such models say that concentrating AI in the hands of a few powerful companies will leave everyone else worse off (a concern that wouldn’t sound out of place among the AI industry's critics on the left, if so many open-source advocates weren’t also venture capitalists who stand to profit when startups can build on cheaper AI without paying Big Tech). items.headline: Nvidia created a weird bit of intrigue by not filing a routine SEC report
items.blurb: One Wall Street analyst got to the bottom of Nvidia's surprise announcement that it wouldn't be filing its formal quarterly results document, the 10-Q, for weeks.
items.text: During Nvidia’s quarterly call on Tuesday, CFO-turned-interim-CEO Colette Kress dropped this little oddity: She said Nvidia wouldn’t be immediately filing its quarterly results report, known as a 10-Q, with the SEC. “We plan to file our 10-Q in the coming weeks.” And she offered no reason why. The delay was widely noticed. Among the many comments on X about it , economic, and investment analyst Edward Dowd called it a “red flag.” Nvidia has typically filed the 10-Q the same day it reports results. The 10-Q offers far more detail about a company’s operations than an earnings press release, including sections that disclose “legal proceedings,” which include lawsuits that could affect the company; and “risk factors” which cover other potentially business-impairing items. The announcement of the delay was so unusual that UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri asked about it after the public earnings call. items.text: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora has blamed AI-assisted cyberattacks and the “deluge of patches” from vendors for some of the technical outages this past week By writing exploit code on the fly and allowing threat actors to probe thousands of targets simultaneously, AI has drastically compressed the time between discovering a flaw and weaponising it Cybersecurity experts believe that Indian enterprises should aggressively upgrade legacy systems, continuously monitor networks and invest in indigenous security products It has been a week of outages. From big tech giants like Microsoft and Apple to JPMorgan Chase and the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), high-profile disruptions at key digital installations exposed how fragile the global digital infrastructure could be . While these incidents have not yet been established as AI-assisted cyberattacks, Nikesh Arora, CEO of Palo Alto Networks, one of the world’s largest cybersecurity companies, said that the events of week were far from a coincidence. “So what the (cybersecurity) industry tried to warn enterprises about six months ago is here. items.text: Physical AI startup Humyn Labs has raised $47 Mn in a funding round, comprising $26 Mn in equity led by Accel and $21 Mn in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton. Humyn claims to have crossed $50 Mn in annualised revenue within six months of starting operations. The startup will use the capital to expand its robot deployment operations to Brazil, South Korea and India, strengthen its data collection hardware. Physical AI startup Humyn Labs has raised $47 Mn (about ₹439 Cr) to expand its data collection and robot deployment operations. The round comprises $26 Mn in Series A equity led by Accel and $21 Mn in venture debt led by Lighthouse Canton, with participation from Trifecta Capital. Other equity investors included Prosus, BeeGlobal, Bajaj Finserv Intelligence, Bajaj Alts AI Opportunities Fund, Dallas Venture Capital, Jump Trading LLC, and angel investor Anita Pramoda. Founded earlier this year by former Nazara CEO Manish Agarwal and Ishank Gupta, Humyn Labs collects data across more than 20 countries. items.headline: Soket AI Raises $4 Mn From Bajaj Finserv To Expand Its AI Model Horizon

items.text: Soket AI has raised $4 Mn (around ₹37 Cr) from Bajaj Finserv's applied research and innovation initiative Finserv Intelligence, and Pennant Technologies Backed by the government's IndiaAI Mission, Soket AI recently launched EKA-1, a 26-Bn-parameter foundation model under Project EKA, its flagship sovereign AI initiative Founded in 2019 by Abhishek Upperwal, Soket AI is building a sovereign open-source AI stack that serves a gamut of Indian languages AI startup Soket AI has raised $4 Mn (around ₹37 Cr) from Bajaj Finserv’s applied research and innovation initiative Finserv Intelligence, and Pennant Technologies. The startup is working on building indigenous foundation models focused on mathematics, coding and reasoning. Bajaj Finance invested approximately $2 Mn in the startup, while Pennant Technologies, an investee company of Bajaj Finance, invested another $2 Mn in the round.
